user.title: Add PieperMonitor
user.description:
Set up the first sensor. Afterwards use 'Add sensor' to add as many sensors as you like, each with its own regions, services and filters.

More about PieperMonitor and the upcoming app: [piepermonitor.nl]({website_url})

data_description.all_services: Shows every P2000 alert in the Netherlands and ignores the region, service, priority and capcode filters. Text filters still apply.
data_description.capcodes: Separate multiple capcodes with a comma or semicolon. An alert matches if any of its capcodes matches.
data_description.include_text: Separate multiple terms with a comma or semicolon; an alert matches if it contains any of them.
data_description.exclude_text: Separate multiple terms with a comma or semicolon; an alert must contain none of them.
data_description.incident_window: How long follow-up alerts are grouped into the same incident.
data_description.vehicles: Call signs from the pager text, for example 24-0733 or 240733. An alert matches if any of these vehicles is alerted.
data_description.radius_km: Only alerts within this distance of your Home Assistant home location. 0 = off. Alerts without a location are dropped when this is set.
data_description.display: What the sensor state shows: the readable alert text or the original pager text.
data_description.priorities: P1 also matches ambulance A1, P2 matches A2 and P3 matches B.

abort.already_configured: PieperMonitor is already added. Use 'Add sensor' for another sensor.

user.title: Follow a capcode or vehicle
user.description: Creates a device with an 'Alarm' event for automations and an 'Active' sensor. It fires as soon as any of the capcodes or vehicles is alerted.

data_description.vehicles: Comma separated call signs, for example 24-0733, 24-3231.
data_description.regions: Optional: empty = all of the Netherlands.
data_description.active_minutes: How long the 'Active' sensor stays on after the last alarm.

reconfigure.title: Change followed units
reconfigure.description: Change the capcodes and vehicles you follow.

data_description.vehicles: Comma separated call signs, for example 24-0733, 24-3231.
data_description.regions: Optional: empty = all of the Netherlands.
data_description.active_minutes: How long the 'Active' sensor stays on after the last alarm.

error.no_units: Enter at least one capcode or vehicle.

init.title: PieperMonitor options

data_description.account_email: The same account as in the PieperMonitor app and on piepermonitor.nl.
data_description.account_password: Only used to log in once; it is not stored. Signed up without a password (social login)? Set one first via 'Forgot password' on piepermonitor.nl.
data_description.account_logout: Removes the account from Home Assistant. Alerts then arrive every 5 minutes.
data_description.source: PieperMonitor gives the same data and interpretation as piepermonitor.nl. Legacy is the previous direct source; it is deprecated and will be removed in a later version.
data_description.brandbase: For fire brigade alerts, looks up the type and post of the alerted vehicles (for example 24-0733 → Tankautospuit, Regionaal) in a public vehicle database. Only regions you receive alerts for, at most once a week.
data_description.scan_interval: How often alerts are fetched, shared by all sensors (30–300 s). Live (Plus or Pro) uses this interval; without Plus or Pro the PieperMonitor source is fetched every 5 minutes.

error.invalid_auth: E-mail or password is not correct.
error.cannot_connect: Could not reach PieperMonitor. Try again later.
error.email_required: Enter the e-mail address of your account.

account_rejected.title: Log in to PieperMonitor again
account_rejected.description: Your PieperMonitor account was not accepted (for example after a password change). Alerts now arrive every 5 minutes. Log in again under Settings > Devices & services > PieperMonitor > Configure.
